mainTopic: A husband waiving his rights to his wife's property, and how such a waiver can work: אירוסין versus נישואין, and adding a קנין
overview: The משנה teaches three levels of a husband giving up his rights to his wife's property. If he waives only 'your property,' he still eats the produce and inherits her, but her sales and gifts are binding. If he adds 'and its produce,' he loses the produce but still inherits her; רבי יהודה says he keeps the 'produce of the produce' unless he waives that too, forever. If he adds 'in your lifetime and after your death,' the תנא קמא says he does not inherit her, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he still inherits, because a condition against what the תורה says is void. The גמרא brings רבי חייא's version, 'one who says,' and then asks how such a waiver can work at all, since a ברייתא says that announcing 'I have no claim on this field' accomplishes nothing. The school of רבי ינאי answers that the husband wrote it while she was an ארוסה, before his rights began, relying on רב כהנא and on רבא's rule that one may refuse a תקנת חכמים, like a wife refusing support and keeping her earnings. When asked why a married husband cannot do the same, אביי says his rights equal hers and רבא says they are stronger, which matters for a שומרת יבם. Finally רב יוסף and רב נחמן argue whether a קנין on such a waiver transfers only the promise or the land itself, and אביי begins to side with רב יוסף, with his reason coming on the next amud.

steps.title: Giving up rights in her property alone changes little
steps.stepSummary: A husband who writes 'I have no claim on your property' still eats its produce while she lives and inherits her when she dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man writes to his wife, 'I have no legal claim or dealings with your property,' he still eats the produce of her property while she is alive, and if she dies, he inherits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first and weakest version of the husband's waiver. It says this waiver does NOT take away his right to the produce or his right to inherit her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband has rights in his wife's property: he eats its produce (פירות) and inherits her if she dies first. Writing only 'your property' (נכסים) is read narrowly. It does not cover the produce, and it does not cover inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I have no legal claim or dealings,' the husband's formula for giving up rights
Property, here the wife's own property
Produce, the yield or income of property (crops, rent, etc.)
He inherits her

phrases.english: One who writes for his wife:
"I have no legal claim or dealings with your property"
he still eats the produce during her lifetime,
phrases.notes: 'Eats the produce' means he gets the income of her fields and other property, not only food.

phrases.english: and if she dies, he inherits her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹתֵב לְאִשְׁתּוֹ דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי בִּנְכָסַיִךְ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A waiver on 'your property' alone does not remove the husband's right to the produce or to inheritance.

steps.title: So what was the point of writing it?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if he keeps the produce and the inheritance, why bother writing the waiver at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did he write for her, 'I have no legal claim or dealings with your property'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself asks a question about the case it just taught. It sets up the next line, which explains what the waiver actually does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the husband kept both main rights, it looks like his words did nothing. The משנה assumes a person's words must have some effect, so it asks what that effect is.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a question that follows from what was just said
Why?

phrases.english: If so, why did he write for her
"I have no legal claim or dealings with your property"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לָמָּה כָּתַב לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what practical effect the waiver in step 1 has.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the waiver accomplishes, if he keeps the produce and the inheritance.

steps.title: The waiver makes her sales and gifts binding
steps.stepSummary: The effect of the waiver: if she sells or gives away her property, the sale or gift stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that if she sold or gave away her property, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. The waiver means the husband cannot cancel her sales or gifts of her property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the waiver, the husband could take back property his wife sold or gave away, because of his rights in it. The waiver gives up exactly that power to block her transactions, nothing more.

keyTerms.meaning: She sold or gave away (as a gift)
Valid, binding, it stands

steps.whatToRemember: Level 1: 'your property' alone means he keeps the produce and the inheritance, but her sales and gifts are binding.

phrases.english: So that if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם מָכְרָה וְנָתְנָה קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The waiver makes the wife's sales and gifts of her property binding against the husband.

steps.title: Giving up the property and its produce
steps.stepSummary: If he writes 'your property and its produce,' he loses the produce during her lifetime but still inherits her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote for her, 'I have no legal claim or dealings with your property or its produce,' he does not eat the produce during her lifetime, but if she dies, he inherits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the second level of waiver, where the husband also mentions the produce. Now he loses the produce, but not the inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each added word takes away only what it names. Mentioning 'produce' removes his right to the produce. It says nothing about after her death, so his inheritance stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Their produce, the produce of her property
He does not eat (he has no right to the produce)

phrases.english: If he wrote for her: "I have no legal claim or dealings
with your property or with its produce"

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹת בְּחַיֶּיהָ,
phrases.english: he does not eat the produce during her lifetime,
but if she dies, he inherits her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לָהּ דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי בִּנְכָסַיִךְ וּבְפֵירוֹתֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger waiver formula than step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiving property and produce removes the produce rights but not the inheritance.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: he still gets the produce of the produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that even after waiving the produce, the husband still eats the 'produce of the produce' unless he waives that too, forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He always eats the produce of the produce, until he writes for her, 'I have no legal claim or dealings with your property, or its produce, or the produce of its produce, forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the second case. He says waiving the produce is not enough to cut off everything, because the produce itself can produce more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the produce belongs to the wife, it becomes her property too. The husband normally eats the yield of her property, so he would eat the yield of that produce ('produce of the produce'). Only an explicit waiver of the produce of the produce, 'forever,' removes this right.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the produce, the yield earned from the produce itself
Always, in every case
Forever

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not arguing about the inheritance. He only argues that the husband keeps a right to the 'produce of the produce' in the second case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He always eats the produce of the produce,
phrases.notes: For example, if the produce is sold and the money buys a field, the crops of that new field.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּכְתּוֹב לַהּ ״דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי
phrases.english: until he writes for her: "I have no legal claim or dealings
with your property, or with its produce,
or with the produce of its produce, forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר לְעוֹלָם אוֹכֵל פֵּירֵי פֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes step 4 by adding a further right the husband keeps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiving the produce does not remove the produce of the produce unless he says so explicitly, forever.

steps.title: Giving up everything, in life and in death
steps.stepSummary: If he waives the property, produce, and produce of produce 'in your lifetime and after your death,' he loses the produce and also does not inherit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote for her, 'I have no legal claim or dealings with your property, its produce, or the produce of its produce, in your lifetime and after your death,' he does not eat the produce during her lifetime, and if she dies, he does not inherit her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third and fullest level of waiver. By mentioning 'after your death,' he also gives up his inheritance, according to the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new words 'and after your death' are what reach the inheritance. Here the תנא קמא treats the inheritance as something the husband can give up, just like the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: In your lifetime and after your death
He does not inherit her
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: If he wrote for her: "I have no legal claim or dealings
with your property, its produce, or the produce of its produce,
in your lifetime and after your death"
he does not eat the produce during her lifetime,
and if she dies, he does not inherit her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לַהּ דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי בִּנְכָסַיִךְ וּבְפֵירוֹתֵיהֶן וּבְפֵירֵי פֵירוֹתֵיהֶן בְּחַיַּיִךְ וּבְמוֹתֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the strongest waiver formula, now covering inheritance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a waiver that includes 'after your death' removes the husband's inheritance.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he still inherits
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the husband still inherits, because a condition against what is written in the תורה is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If she dies, he inherits her, because he is making a condition against what is written in the תורה, and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the תורה, his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the last ruling of the תנא קמא. He holds that the husband's waiver of inheritance does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning shows he views the husband's inheritance as a rule written in the תורה. A private condition cannot cancel a תורה rule, so the condition about inheritance is void and the husband inherits.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a condition against what is written in the תורה
His condition is void
He will inherit her

steps.whatToRemember: Level 3: the full waiver 'in life and death' removes inheritance for the תנא קמא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it cannot, because a condition against the תורה is void.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'כל המתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה תנאו בטל' is a general principle about the limits of private agreements, and it appears across ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If she dies, he inherits her,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: because he is making a condition against what is written in the Torah,
phrases.notes: He means the husband's right to inherit his wife, which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sees as a תורה law.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אִם מֵתָה יִירָשֶׁנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the inheritance ruling of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband inherits despite the waiver, because a condition against the תורה is void.

steps.title: רבי חייא's version: 'one who says'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting רבי חייא's teaching, which reads 'one who SAYS to his wife' instead of the משנה's 'one who WRITES.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חייא taught: 'One who says to his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא from רבי חייא with slightly different wording from our משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says 'writes' (הכותב), but רבי חייא says 'says' (האומר). The change suggests that the waiver may work even when only spoken, without a written document. The next step then asks a more basic question: how can such a waiver, written or spoken, work at all?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
One who says (verbally)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not skip over the small wording change. The whole point of quoting רבי חייא is the switch from 'writes' to 'says.'

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Chiya taught:
"One who says to his wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא whose wording differs from the opening of the משנה in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא's ברייתא speaks of a husband who 'says' the waiver, which suggests that a spoken waiver may also work.

steps.title: How can a waiver like this work at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: a ברייתא says that declaring 'I have no dealings with this field' accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote this to her, what does it accomplish? A ברייתא teaches that someone who tells his fellow 'I have no claim on this field, no involvement with it, my hands are removed from it' has said nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's case of a husband who writes off his rights to his wife's property. A ברייתא says such statements are meaningless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that just announcing you are pulling away from property does not remove your rights. If so, the husband's written statement in the משנה should also be empty words. Yet the משנה treats it as working.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no legal claim or dealings
My hands are removed (I withdraw)
He has said nothing; the statement has no legal effect

phrases.english: And if he wrote this to her,
what of it?
phrases.notes: He means: how could writing this actually take away his rights?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who says to his fellow

phrases.aramaic: ״דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ״,
phrases.english: "I have no legal claim or dealings over this field,"
"and I have no involvement with it,"
"and my hands are removed from it"
— has not said anything!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כְּתַב לַהּ הָכִי, מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic workability of the waiver described in the משנה (Steps 4 and 6).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that a husband's waiver ('דין ודברים אין לי') takes effect at all: making her sales binding, removing the produce, or removing inheritance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says that statements of withdrawal from property have no legal effect, so the husband's waiver should also be void.

steps.title: He wrote it while she was still an ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the משנה is talking about a waiver written during אירוסין, based on רב כהנא's rule about a future inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: the משנה is talking about one who writes this to her while she is still an ארוסה. This follows רב כהנא, who said: an inheritance that comes to a person from somewhere else can be stipulated away, so that he will not inherit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The husband wrote the waiver before the rights were his, while she was only an ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about giving up something you already own, which does not work. During אירוסין, the husband's rights to her property have not yet started. רב כהנא teaches that a right that will come to you later can be turned down ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ינאי
A betrothed woman, before נישואין
An inheritance coming from another source (not yet his)
Makes a condition or stipulation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is wrong. It is about rights a person already holds. This answer works only because the husband's rights had not yet begun.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
It is where he writes to her while she is still betrothed,
in line with Rav Kahana.
For Rav Kahana said:
An inheritance that comes to a person
from another place
phrases.notes: Like a husband inheriting from his wife: it does not come to him directly through his own family line.

phrases.english: — a person may stipulate about it that he will not inherit it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: בְּכוֹתֵב לָהּ וְעוֹדָהּ אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the משנה's case to the time of אירוסין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about a married husband giving up rights he already holds, which the ברייתא says is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a husband who wrote this while she was an ארוסה, when the rights were not yet his. Turning down a future right works, as רב כהנא says.

steps.title: Second support: רבא lets a person turn down a rabbinic benefit
steps.stepSummary: The answer also relies on רבא: a person who says he does not want a rabbinic enactment made for him is listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it follows רבא, who said: one who says, 'I do not want a rabbinic enactment like this one,' we listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי adds a second foundation to their answer, the rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's right to the produce of his wife's property is a תקנת חכמים made for his benefit. רבא teaches that someone may refuse such a benefit. Together with רב כהנא, this explains why the husband's waiver can work.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not want
An enactment of the Sages
Such as this one
We listen to him (his refusal works)

phrases.english: and in line with Rava.
For Rava said:
One who says: "I do not want
an ordinance of the Sages such as this one"
— we listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרָבָא. דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 10 by adding a second source, רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional support for the same answer
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband can refuse the rabbinic benefit of the produce, as רבא says, and this is in addition to רב כהנא's rule.

steps.title: What does 'such as this one' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which enactment רבא was pointing to with the words 'such as this one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'such as this one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבא's words. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said 'such as this one' as though pointing to a specific enactment. The גמרא wants to know which example he meant, so that we understand what kind of enactment can be refused.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What is meant by "such as this one"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּגוֹן זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in רבא's teaching from Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rabbinic enactment רבא had in mind with 'such as this one'

steps.title: The example: a wife may refuse support and keep her earnings
steps.stepSummary: רבא meant רב הונא's teaching in the name of רב: a wife can say 'I will not be supported, and I will not work for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב הונא in the name of רב. רב הונא said in the name of רב: a woman may say to her husband, 'I will not be fed by you, and I will not work for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא was referring to רב הונא's ruling about a wife giving up her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set up an arrangement: the husband supports his wife, and in return he receives her earnings. Since this was made mainly for her benefit, she may refuse it. This is the model case of turning down a תקנת חכמים, and the husband's right to the produce works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Being supported or fed (by the husband)
Working (giving her earnings to the husband)
רב הונא quoting his teacher רב

phrases.english: Like that of Rav Huna, who said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A woman is able to say to her husband:
"I will not be supported, and I will not work."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב. דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Such as this one' refers to the enactment of support in exchange for earnings, which a wife may refuse, as רב הונא said in the name of רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the model for when a person may refuse a תקנת חכמים: when it was made for that person's own benefit.

steps.title: If so, a married husband should also be able to waive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if רבא's rule is true, why limit the case to an ארוסה? Even a married husband should be able to refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even when she is already married, it should also work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of the school of רבי ינאי. If רבא's rule is enough, then why say the משנה is only about an ארוסה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule seems to let anyone refuse a rabbinic benefit at any time. If that is so, the limit to the time of אירוסין looks unnecessary. A married husband should be able to waive the produce as well, and the ברייתא would not be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A fully married woman (after נישואין)
Also

phrases.english: If that is so,
even a married woman too?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ נְשׂוּאָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Steps 10 and 11 by using רבא's rule against the limit to אירוסין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The school of רבי ינאי's limit of the משנה to an ארוסה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא allows anyone to refuse a rabbinic benefit, then a married husband could refuse the produce too, so there is no need to limit the case to אירוסין.

steps.title: אביי: A married husband's rights equal his wife's
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a married husband cannot waive, because his hold on her property is equal to hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For a married woman, his hand is like her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 14. אביי explains why a married husband cannot simply refuse his rights the way an ארוס can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After נישואין, the husband is like a full partner in his wife's property. His rights are not just a future hope that he can turn down with words. So saying 'I have no claim' does not remove him, and the case had to be about an ארוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: A fully married woman (after נישואין)
His hand is like her hand: his rights in her property equal hers

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A married woman: his hand is like her hand.
phrases.notes: 'Hand' here means his ownership rights in her property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְשׂוּאָה — יָדוֹ כְּיָדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any husband could refuse the enactment, like in רבא's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A married husband is already a partner in the property, so a verbal waiver cannot remove him

steps.title: רבא: A married husband's rights are even greater than hers
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a stronger version of the answer: the husband's rights in her property outweigh hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: His hand is stronger than her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own version of the answer to the same challenge. He says the married husband's hold on the property is even stronger than the wife's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אביי and רבא agree that a married husband cannot waive with words. They disagree only on how strong his rights are: equal to hers, or greater than hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Better or stronger

phrases.english: Rava said:
His hand is stronger than her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: יָדוֹ עֲדִיפָא מִיָּדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different strength level than אביי for the same answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same distinction as אביי, with a stronger claim for the husband
steps.terutzMaskana: The married husband's rights outweigh the wife's, so he certainly cannot waive with words

steps.title: Where אביי and רבא's views make a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the argument matters for a widow waiting for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is for a woman waiting for her brother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the argument between אביי and רבא actually changes the law: the case of a שומרת יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבם has weaker rights than a husband. If the husband's rights are greater than hers (רבא), the יבם's rights can still be at least equal to hers. If the husband's rights only equal hers (אביי), the יבם's rights fall below hers.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of a dispute
A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום

phrases.english: The practical difference is for a woman waiting for her brother-in-law.
phrases.notes: A widow without children waits for her late husband's brother, who may marry her through יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לְשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical result of the אביי and רבא argument
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between אביי and רבא matters for the rights of a יבם in a שומרת יבם's property
steps.whatToRemember: A married husband cannot drop his rights with words. That is why the waiver case is set during אירוסין. אביי and רבא argue only about how strong his rights are.

steps.title: What if the waiver was backed by a קנין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what happens if, besides saying 'I have no claim,' a formal act of acquisition was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If they made a קנין from him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. A plain verbal waiver doesn't do much, so what if a formal קנין was done with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about how far a קנין reaches when it is added to a waiver. Does it only lock in the promise, or does it actually transfer the property? The next two steps give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
They made a formal act of acquisition (קנין) from him

phrases.english: They asked:
If they made a קנין from him, what is the law?
phrases.notes: A קנין done along with words like the ones in the ברייתא from step 9: 'I have no claim or dealings with this field.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: קָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a plain waiver to a waiver backed by a קנין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קנין added to a waiver transfers the land or only strengthens the promise

steps.title: רב יוסף: The קנין covers only the promise
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the קנין locks in only the words 'I have no claim', not the land itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They acquired from him only the 'no claim or dealings' promise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. The קנין only covers the promise that he would have no claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the קנין is only as strong as the words it was made on. Since the words only said 'I have no dealings,' the קנין adds nothing beyond that. The land itself does not change hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal claim and involvement: the 'I have no claim' formula

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From claims and dealings they acquired from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִדִּין וּדְבָרִים קָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the שאלה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קנין covers only the promise of 'no claim', so it is no stronger than the promise

steps.title: רב נחמן: The קנין transfers the land itself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the קנין works fully and transfers the actual land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They acquired the land itself from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees with רב יוסף. He holds that the קנין actually transfers the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the קנין is not limited to the words 'I have no claim.' It takes hold of the land itself, so it works as a true transfer of the land, not just a promise.

keyTerms.meaning: The land itself, its actual ownership

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
From the land itself they acquired from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: מִגּוּפָהּ שֶׁל קַרְקַע קָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רב יוסף's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קנין fully transfers ownership of the land

steps.title: אביי sides with רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב יוסף's view makes more sense. His reason comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רב יוסף's statement makes sense.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes a side in the argument and supports רב יוסף. This line sets up the reason, which the גמרא gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only אביי's opening judgment. His proof for why רב יוסף is more reasonable comes on the next amud, so don't treat this as the final word.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is reasonable

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The statement of Rav Yosef makes sense

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתָא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב יוסף's side in the argument and leads into a reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי holds that רב יוסף's view, that the קנין covers only the promise, is more reasonable
